title: Lanternwake

seeds.dusk: Supper is on. The lamps are still out there, if you are the one who tends them.
seeds.moonrise: The street goes silver and nobody knocks this late. Sit; the fire is yours.
seeds.deep-night: Deep-night is for the desperate and the loved. You look like both.
seeds.first-light: Grey on the water already. The bread is hot; eat before you walk.

seeds.dusk: Iron keeps the day's heat a while yet. Like people.
seeds.moonrise: Cold enough to make the anvil sing. I mend what the coast breaks.
seeds.deep-night: The fire is the only clock I keep. It says: still night.
seeds.first-light: I made the first lamp-hook the Guild ever issued. Yours should hang here when you are done.

seeds.dusk: Light one if you can spare it. The dark is polite, mostly.
seeds.moonrise: I used to say the Hush was judgment. The candles never agreed with me.
seeds.deep-night: The deep-night burns the shortest. Every candle here says the same thing.
seeds.first-light: First light is the shrine's favourite hour. The flames look embarrassed.

seeds.dusk: One page a day, ten years, and the Guild stands again. On paper. Paper first.
seeds.moonrise: The moon is very good for reading by and terrible for accounts.
seeds.deep-night: Even the ink sleeps at deep-night. I keep the pens warm.
seeds.first-light: New day, new column. The coast is solvent again in principle.

seeds.dusk: I ran the whole road twice today and the day is not even done!
seeds.moonrise: Nobody needs anything at moonrise. It is very boring. Tell me something!
seeds.deep-night: Deep-night is just the day hiding. I am not fooled.
seeds.first-light: FIRST LIGHT! I already told four people and a gull!

seeds.dusk: Sky says quiet. Water says later. The two of them never agree before supper.
seeds.moonrise: Moon pulls the tide wide. Keep to the high road tonight.
seeds.deep-night: High water at deep-night, like always. The causeway walks under it and remembers.
seeds.first-light: Grey-gold on the sea. Good weather for walking and better for lamplighters.

seeds.dusk: A mended net is stronger where it broke. People less so.
seeds.moonrise: I keep thinking the fire was someone's fault. It is easier that way. It may not be true.
seeds.deep-night: My brother went into the dark and came back kind and empty. I mend. It is what is left.
seeds.first-light: The light is honest in the morning. It makes me honest too, unhappily.

seeds.dusk: Count the lamps, count the wounded, count the days. It is how I sleep.
seeds.moonrise: Evidence or it is superstition. I have been wrong before. Spectacularly.
seeds.deep-night: I do not sleep at deep-night. I count things until the count gets tired.
seeds.first-light: Ten years ago I wrote 'the Master is dead' in a ledger. I would like to cross it out.

seeds.dusk: The town is quiet and quiet is safe. Mostly. Do not quote me.
seeds.moonrise: I shut the road for ten years to keep this town safe. It is possible I overdid it.
seeds.deep-night: Nothing stirs at deep-night. That is when I do my worrying.
seeds.first-light: A reeve is only a person with a list and a lamp. Speaking of lamps...

seeds.dusk: Mrrp.
seeds.moonrise: Mrrp.
seeds.deep-night: Mrrp.
seeds.first-light: Mrrp.

seeds.dusk: Crossing is free at dusk. At deep-night it costs you getting wet.
seeds.moonrise: Tin lanterns up and down the road. Mine never go out. Stubbornness counts as oil.
seeds.deep-night: The causeway is under the water now. Walk it anyway. The road knows where it is.
seeds.first-light: I have crossed a thousand times and the sea has not taken me yet. Today looks promising too.

seeds.dusk: I pole quiet at dusk so the water can talk.
seeds.moonrise: The bell sings under the water tonight. It is not a sad song, whatever the priest says.
seeds.deep-night: Everyone asks what the dark sounds like. Waves. Just waves. And the bell.
seeds.first-light: First light is when the fish come up to look at the sky. I see them.

seeds.dusk: Marsh at dusk: mind the pans, mind the quiet, mind your own feet.
seeds.moonrise: Sable says the marsh is safe if you sing. Sable is half right. Sing anyway.
seeds.deep-night: The Master went down there. I will keep saying it until someone believes me.
seeds.first-light: The mist says what the night did. The mist says: nothing. Good.

seeds.dusk: Sing while you walk. The Hush hates a tune. Probably.
seeds.moonrise: Wren says I sing too much. The pans say otherwise and I trust the pans.
seeds.deep-night: At deep-night I sing louder. Somebody has to.
seeds.first-light: The reeds go gold at first light. For about four minutes. It is worth being up.

seeds.dusk: I have lived long enough to outlast two truths and one lie. The lie is winning.
seeds.moonrise: Ask what happened to the bell. Ask Hobb. Ask anyone - just not the priest. Not yet.
seeds.deep-night: The dark took my sister's name. She smiles at me now like a neighbour. I keep the name for her.
seeds.first-light: The Master lives. Ten years of being laughed at and I am still right.

seeds.dusk: The chandlery keeps oil, rope and blunt opinions. All three are sound.
seeds.moonrise: My brother is dead. I have said it so long it tastes like nothing. I would like it to be false.
seeds.deep-night: A lightship never sleeps. I am retired. I never sleep. Same thing.
seeds.first-light: Buy rope before you walk, lampwright. The sea eats rope the way the dark eats names.

seeds.dusk: I can splice a wick faster than anyone on this cliff. Prove me wrong. Please.
seeds.moonrise: Aunt Orra says the Guild is over. Then I say 'wicks' and she stops talking.
seeds.deep-night: I keep the practice lamps trimmed at deep-night. When the Guild comes back I will be ready.
seeds.first-light: The cliff lamp is still lit. Good. That is my future burning nicely.

seeds.dusk: The bell was holy and the sea has it. I have made my peace badly.
seeds.moonrise: I say the Hush is judgment because the alternative is grief. I know how that sounds.
seeds.deep-night: I pray at deep-night for my friend. Whichever one of them is still alive.
seeds.first-light: Some mornings the light feels like an answer. Most mornings it is just weather.

seeds.dusk: Gulls come in at dusk in threes. Never fours. Do not ask me why.
seeds.moonrise: The gulls say the weald lamp is lit. Gulls do not lie. They have no reason to.
seeds.deep-night: Nothing flies at deep-night except the Hush and it flies badly.
seeds.first-light: The Master's name? The gulls know it. They just refuse to say it in mixed company.

seeds.dusk: I make what the sea eats. Business is steady, which is a sad sentence.
seeds.moonrise: Rope remembers being twisted. So do people. I try to twist gently.
seeds.deep-night: No ropemaking at deep-night. The strands judge you.
seeds.first-light: Take a coil. You will need it where you are going. Everyone needs it where they are going.

seeds.dusk: The sea gives back everything it takes. Bones, names, rope. Slowly. On its own terms.
seeds.moonrise: I name the ribs. That one is Patience. The tall one is Regret. They like it.
seeds.deep-night: The tide breathes in and out of the cave like something sleeping. I do not wake it.
seeds.first-light: New shingle in the night. Someone's cargo. Someone's grief. I will name it by noon.

seeds.dusk: The weald closes one eye at dusk. The other one stays open. Mind the other one.
seeds.moonrise: The trees lean toward the lamp clearing. Trees do not lean for nothing.
seeds.deep-night: The weald is waking up. I do not know into what. I keep the axe close and the lamp closer.
seeds.first-light: Crows say the way is open to the barrow. Crows are great gossips and rarely wrong.

seeds.dusk: Down is dark and down is long, but down is where the road was first.
seeds.moonrise: The dead keep the road. They charge nothing and they complain less than the living.
seeds.deep-night: Cold stone, warm candles. Someone keeps the deep road lit. It is not the dead.
seeds.first-light: Up is morning and down is truth. Most days I would pick down.

seeds.dusk: I sing the bell a hymn at dusk. It remembers the words. I only remember the tune.
seeds.moonrise: The sea stands in the aisles at moonrise. It is very polite about it.
seeds.deep-night: The Warden walks at deep-night. He is so tired. Someone should tell him to sit.
seeds.first-light: The light comes into the nave sideways, like an apology. I like it.

seeds.dusk: I cut the bell down. I have said it every dusk for ten years to an empty nave.
seeds.moonrise: The dark was supposed to scold me. It never did. That is worse.
seeds.deep-night: My sister keeps the chandlery. My friend keeps the deep road. I keep nothing well.
seeds.first-light: If the lamp were lit... no. It is not my light to ask for.

seeds.dusk: I keep the road lit in the dark. I do not know why. The candles seem to.
seeds.moonrise: A name is a lamp too. I had one once, I think. It was warm.
seeds.deep-night: Every night I light the dark and every night the dark forgets me. It is a fair trade.
seeds.first-light: The Beacon knows me. I am beginning to think it always did.

seeds.dusk: The house keeps the Beacon's tools and one extra cup. It has kept the cup ten years.
seeds.moonrise: My nieces say the Master walks the deep road. I keep the cup out anyway.
seeds.deep-night: From up here the dark looks like a sea and the lamps look like boats.
seeds.first-light: The kettle is on. Whoever comes home today comes home to heat.

vault_intro: The Lanternwake ledger: what the coast keeps, and what it owes.
